title: Nocturne setup assistant
intro: We will help you get Nocturne working, one step at a time.
failed: Check the setup steps below, then restart this app.
demo: Preview: no connection to your Home Assistant.
step_dns: 4. Make the address work at home
domain_help: Use a domain name you control. Keep it after creating your account: passkeys depend on it.
duck_help: Create a name at duckdns.org. Install DuckDNS in Home Assistant → Settings → Apps. Enter your full domain and token in DuckDNS, not here. Enable Let's Encrypt after reading and accepting its terms. Choose fullchain.pem and privkey.pem. Start DuckDNS and check its log for successful certificate creation. For tenants created at any time, request one certificate covering both mynocturne.duckdns.org and *.mynocturne.duckdns.org. Replace the example name with yours. Configure wildcard DNS too; no individual tenant list is needed. Keep this app on the base-domain URL.
certificate_help: In this app's Configuration enter the certificate filename fullchain.pem and private key filename privkey.pem. Enter your HTTPS domain with port 8448 for Stable or 8449 for Main. Use your configured host port if different. Keep /ssl read-only. No change to Home Assistant Core HTTPS is needed.
dns_help: Your device must resolve the same domain to your Home Assistant address. Use local DNS (split DNS) or a router supporting NAT loopback. DuckDNS alone may point to your public address. Check Wi-Fi on a phone as well. DNS certificate validation does not require exposing Nocturne to the internet.
finish_help: Restart this app after saving the settings. Open your HTTPS address in a new tab. The browser must show no certificate warning. Complete Nocturne's account/passkey setup and test a second device.
restart: Save settings in Home Assistant, then restart this app.
renew: DuckDNS checks certificate renewal while running. If using the separate Let's Encrypt app, schedule regular starts to check renewal. Choose one certificate manager; do not let two overwrite the same files.
existing: Already have a certificate? Reuse the matching chain and key; keep your existing certificate manager. DuckDNS is optional.
gateway_login: Gateway username: nocturne. Use the access code below as the password. Your Nocturne account is a separate sign-in.
yaml_help: Select the example text and copy it into the matching certificate app’s YAML configuration. Replace the example domain and token. These are partial examples: keep your other settings. Use one certificate manager. In the visual Let’s Encrypt DNS field, paste only provider and duckdns_token, without dns:.
monitor_title: What is available in Home Assistant
monitor_help: Open Settings → Devices & services → Home Assistant Supervisor → your Nocturne Stable or Main device. Show disabled entities, open CPU Percent and Memory Percent, and enable them in entity settings. You can also enable Version and Latest version. Then add the enabled sensors to your dashboard. Entity IDs depend on your installation.
monitor_scope: CPU and memory measure this whole container: API, web, PostgreSQL and nginx together. They are not separate service metrics or medical readings. Use the app’s Information page for current usage, Configuration for options and Log for startup errors. The setup assistant does not fetch or display live usage; stopped apps may have unavailable statistics.
error_CERT_FILES:
Open the certificate manager’s Log and confirm successful issuance.
In Nocturne Configuration, enter fullchain.pem and privkey.pem (or your actual filenames). Both files must exist in /ssl.
error_CERT_HOSTNAME:
Keep public_url on the intended base domain.
Request a certificate containing that base name and its *. wildcard for tenants, then check the issued certificate’s SAN names.
error_CERT_SAN:
The certificate needs DNS names under Subject Alternative Name (SAN); a Common Name alone is insufficient.
Ask the certificate manager to issue a new pair with the base name and its *. wildcard.
error_CERT_KEY_MISMATCH:
The certificate and private key do not belong together.
Select both files from the same successful issuance; restore or reissue the pair at the certificate manager. Do not mix an old key with a new certificate.
error_CERT_EXPIRED:
Open the certificate manager’s Log and fix failed renewal.
DuckDNS renews while running; the separate Let’s Encrypt app needs scheduled starts. Verify a new certificate was issued.
error_CERT_NOT_YET_VALID:
Check Home Assistant’s system date/time and timezone.
Check the certificate’s start date; use a currently valid pair if it is still in the future.
error_SETUP_REQUIRED:
Open this app’s Configuration and correct the domain, port and certificate filenames.
Open this app’s Log for the startup error. Keep existing data and keys; do not uninstall or reset the database.
gateway_fallback: The app is available with the gateway code still enabled; the request to disable it could not yet be confirmed.
gateway_setup: Sign in through the gateway using username nocturne and the displayed code. Complete Nocturne’s owner/account setup, then save gateway_auth: false and restart.
gateway_recovery: Keep the gateway on and complete Nocturne account recovery. Restore the matching backup if needed; do not reset data or keys.
gateway_check: Check the code above and the app Log: runtime/status/demo or anonymous-data denial could not be confirmed. Review Nocturne access/share settings. Both normal data routes must refuse anonymous access (401). Keep the gateway on until this check passes.
skip_gateway_help: Only with gateway_auth off. Skip the wrapper authentication check for intentional anonymous access; Nocturne access/share settings still decide permissions. Default off. Save and restart.
gateway_skipped: Gateway check deliberately skipped. Nocturne access/share settings decide anonymous access. To restore checks, turn skip_gateway_check off and restart.
